questions.stem:
*Superbounce* is a manufacturer of tennis balls.

It knows from past records that 10% of its tennis balls fail a bounce test.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the probability that from a random sample of 10 of these tennis balls

(i) at least 4 fail the bounce test

(ii) more than 1 but fewer than 5 fail the bounce test.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a)(i) $X \sim \mathrm{B}(10, 0.1)$
$\mathrm{P}(X \geqslant 4) = 1-\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 3) = 1-0.9872$ M1
$= 0.0128$ awrt 0.0128 A1

(ii) $\mathrm{P}(1<X<5) = \mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 4)-\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 1) = 0.9984-0.7361$
or $\mathrm{P}(X=2)+\mathrm{P}(X=3)+\mathrm{P}(X=4) = 0.1937+0.0574+0.0112$ M1
$= 0.2623$ awrt 0.262 A1

Notes:
(i) M1: for writing or using $\mathrm{P}(X \geqslant 4) = 1-\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 3)$
A1: awrt 0.0128
(ii) M1: for writing or using $\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 4)-\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 1)$ or for writing or using $\mathrm{P}(X=2)+\mathrm{P}(X=3)+\mathrm{P}(X=4)$
A1: awrt 0.262

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The managing director makes changes to the production process and claims that these changes will reduce the probability of its tennis balls failing the bounce test.

After the changes were made a random sample of 50 of the tennis balls were tested and it was found that 2 failed the bounce test.

(b) Test, at the 5% significance level, whether or not this result supports the managing director's claim.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\mathrm{H_0}: p=0.1$ $\mathrm{H_1}: p<0.1$ B1
$X \sim \mathrm{B}(50, 0.1)$
$\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 2) = 0.1117$ or CR $X \leqslant 1$ B1
Do not reject $\mathrm{H_0}$/Not in the critical region M1
There is insufficient evidence to suggest that this result supports the managing director's claim/not enough evidence to suggest a reduction in the probability of a tennis ball failing the bounce test A1

Notes:
B1: Both hypotheses correct. Must be in terms of $p$ or $\pi$. Must be attached to $\mathrm{H_0}$ and $\mathrm{H_1}$
B1: awrt 0.112 or CR $X \leqslant 1$
M1: A correct ft statement consistent with their p-value and 0.05 or their CR and 2 - no context needed but do not allow contradicting non contextual comments. The comparison of their p-value and the significance level is not counted as a non contextual statement.
May be implied by a correct ft conclusion in context.
A1: Correct conclusion in context which must be not rejecting $\mathrm{H_0}$. Must use underlined words (oe). No hypotheses then A0
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: Must have a p-value or CR to access this mark.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
In a second random sample of $n$ tennis balls it was found that none failed the bounce test. As a result of this sample, the managing director's claim is supported at the 1% significance level.

(c) Find the smallest possible value of $n$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $X \sim \mathrm{B}(n, 0.1)$ and we reject $\mathrm{H_0}$ if $\mathrm{P}(X=0)<0.01$
$\mathrm{P}(X=0) = \left[{}^n C_0 \times 0.1^0\right] \times 0.9^n [<0.01]$ M1
$0.9^{44} = 0.00969... [<0.01]$ or $n > \dfrac{\ln 0.01}{\ln 0.9} \Rightarrow n>43.7$ M1
$n = 44$ A1

Notes:
M1: For recognising $\mathrm{P}(X=0)=0.9^n$
M1: For $0.9^{44}(=0.00969...)$ or $0.9^{43}(=0.01077...)$ or rearranging to $n>\dfrac{\ln 0.01}{\ln 0.9}$ ... (Allow =)
$n>$ awrt 43.7 implies M1M1 (Allow $n=$ awrt 43.7 for M1M1)
A1: Cao
SC: Use of tables only, $n=40, p=0.0148$ and $n=50, p=0.0052$ scores M1M0A0

parts.label: a
parts.reason: Poisson is a named concept not mentioned anywhere in the 9MA0 statements (only binomial and Normal distributions are covered in S4.1/S4.2); therefore this part is out.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: This part asks for an assumption underlying the Poisson model identified in (a); since Poisson itself is not a spec topic, this part only makes sense after an out-of-spec part and is therefore out.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.reason: Requires calculating P(X>4) for X~Po(4); Poisson distribution is not mentioned in any 9MA0 statement, so this is out.

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.reason: Builds on the Poisson probability from (i); Poisson not in spec, so out.

parts.label: d
parts.reason: S5.1-S5.3 cover hypothesis tests for binomial proportion and Normal mean only; no statement covers testing a Poisson rate. Also depends on Poisson distribution from (a)/(c), an out-of-spec topic.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Listing combinations for a sampling distribution
parts.reason: This sets up the sampling distribution of the sample mean of 3 coins, a topic ('sampling distribution') not mentioned in any 9MA0 statement; the whole question builds toward this out-of-spec concept, so out.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: Requires reading off values a, b from the sampling distribution table of X̄, a concept not covered in the specification.

parts.label: c
parts.reason: Although finding p and q from p^3 and q^3 uses basic algebra, it is embedded in and only meaningful within the out-of-spec sampling-distribution context; it uses information (the given table entries) that only makes sense after the out-of-spec setup in (a)/(b).

parts.label: d
parts.reason: Continues to build the sampling distribution of X̄ using binomial-type probabilities; sampling distributions of a statistic are not a 9MA0 topic, so out.

parts.label: e
parts.reason: Explicitly requires the 'sampling distribution' of M, a term not present in any 9MA0 statement, so out.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: S4.2 explicitly states 'Knowledge of the probability density function is not required'; this part uses a given pdf diagram directly, so out.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: Requires manipulating a probability density function, explicitly excluded by S4.2.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.technique: E(X) for continuous random variable via pdf
parts.reason: Calculating E(X) from a pdf by integration; S4.2 excludes knowledge of the pdf and its derivations, and no statement covers integration to find E(X)/Var(X) of a continuous distribution.

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.technique: Var(X) for continuous random variable via pdf
parts.reason: Same exclusion as above applies (S4.2), plus depends on the out-of-spec pdf setup.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: E(A) for function of continuous random variable via pdf integration
parts.reason: Requires integrating a pdf and using E(X), E(X^2), both excluded/not covered per S4.2, and depends on earlier out-of-spec parts.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: Requires X~Po(5); Poisson distribution is not mentioned in any 9MA0 statement, so out.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Binomial probability using a Poisson-derived probability
parts.reason: Although the binomial calculation method itself is in spec (S4.1), this part depends on the Poisson probability computed in the out-of-spec part (a), so it only makes sense after an out-of-spec part.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Normal approximation to Poisson, standardising and solving for parameter
parts.reason: Requires modelling defects as Poisson then approximating with Normal; Poisson is not a 9MA0 topic and the specific Poisson-to-Normal approximation is not mentioned (S4.2 only covers binomial-to-Normal approximation), so out.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: Requires working with a cumulative distribution function of a continuous random variable; S4.2 excludes derivation of the cdf and knowledge of the pdf, and no statement covers general cdf manipulation, so out.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Deriving f(x) from F(x) and finding E(X) by integration
parts.reason: Requires differentiating a cdf to get a pdf and integrating xf(x) to find E(X); pdf knowledge and derivation are explicitly excluded by S4.2, so out.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Finding Var(X) via integration of x^2 f(x)
parts.reason: Same exclusion applies (S4.2 excludes pdf knowledge/derivation); also builds on out-of-spec part (b).

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Solving simultaneous equations from (b) and (c) for k
parts.reason: Depends entirely on results from out-of-spec parts (b) and (c) involving the pdf/cdf, so out.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Finding constants a, b from k
parts.reason: Depends on out-of-spec part (d) and the underlying pdf/cdf framework, so out.
